en: Listen to this Purana of five marks, O mighty-armed one. Hearing it, a person, O king, is freed from the sin of killing a Brahmin.

first: पर्वाणि चात्र वै पञ्च कीर्तितानि स्वयम्भुवा ।
en: Five sections of it were declared by the self-born Brahma. The first is called Brahma, the second is remembered as Vaishnava.
The third is called Shaiva, the fourth is called Tvashtra, and the fifth is named Pratisarga, honoured by all the worlds.

first: एतानि तात पर्वाणि लक्षणानि निबोध मे ।
en: Learn from me, my dear, the marks of these sections: creation, secondary creation, lineages, the ages of the Manus,
and the deeds of the lineages. This is the Purana of five marks, adorned with the fourteen branches of learning, O joy of the Kurus.
The six Vedangas, the four Vedas, Mimamsa, the wide science of logic, the Purana and the law books: these are the fourteen branches of learning.
Medicine, archery and music are those three; the science of wealth is the fourth. These make the eighteen branches of learning.
First, the creation of beings is told here in full. Hearing it, one is freed from sin and attains the highest peace.
In the beginning, my dear, the world was dark, without any mark, unknowable, beyond reasoning, as if fast asleep on every side.
Then that lord, unmanifest, showing forth this world and the great elements, rose up, mighty and dispelling the darkness.
He who is beyond the senses, cannot be grasped, is subtle, unmanifest and eternal, made of all beings and beyond thought, rose up by himself.

first: योऽसौ षड्विंशको लोके तथा यः पुरुषोत्तमः ।
en: He who is the twenty-sixth principle in the world, who is the best of persons, the sun, O mighty-armed one, is also called the supreme Brahman.
Wishing to create many kinds of creatures, he thought on them and first created from his own body; in them he placed his seed.
That from which everything is born, with gods, demons and men, is called seed, semen and fierce potency.
These are the names of that seed, told by the self-born one. It became a golden egg, O lord, surrounded by a garland of flames.
In it Brahma himself was born, grandfather of all the worlds, eldest of the gods, four-faced, the supreme one, the grandfather.
Knower of the field, the Person, the creator, Shambhu and Narayana: by such synonymous words Brahma is praised.
The wise always call him Virinchi and the lotus-born. The waters are called "nara", for the waters are the children of the Person.

first: ता यदस्यायनं पूर्वं तेन नारायणः स्मृतः ।
en: Because they were his first resting place, he is remembered as Narayana. The poets fixed the word "ara" for speed.
The waters themselves became an ocean, and so they are very swift. The unmanifest cause, eternal, both being and non-being,

first: तद्विसृष्टः स पुरुषो लोके ब्रह्मेति कीर्त्त्यते ।
en: released by that, the Person is called Brahma in the world. Thus the lord, having understood the truth within the egg, entered meditation, O best of kings, and split that egg in two. From the two halves he made heaven and earth.
Between them he made the sky, the eight directions and the place of the waters. The great one went upward, O king, to bring the worlds into being on every side.
From the great principle came the sense of self, and from that the three qualities as well. The three qualities are very subtle, understood only by the mind, O descendant of Bharata.
They are the cause of the birth of the great elements, O king. From them the five senses were slowly taken.
In the same way, the subtle parts of the six mighty ones of boundless power [were formed].
Having placed them in the measures of himself, the lord, the all-pervading one, made all beings in due order, my dear.
The subtle parts of whose form are these six supports; therefore the wise call it his body and his form.

first: महान्ति तानि भूतानि आविशन्ति ततो विभुम् ।
en: Those great elements then enter the all-pervading lord, together with action, and the qualities too with their own qualities.
From these seven mighty persons, from the subtle forms alone, the imperishable one gives rise to this pair.
From the great principle and the origin of the elements, by which this world is pervaded, there are only five persons, O mighty-armed one.
Some wise men, my dear, wish for the higher creation in this way, and other thinkers, O mighty-armed one, declare it likewise.
That supreme self, my dear, at the start of an age creates a body and, wishing to create many kinds of creatures, makes birth.

first: तेन सृष्टः पुद्गलस्तु प्रधानं विशते नृप ।
en: The being created by him enters the Primal Nature, O king. Stirred by him, the Primal Nature produces many changes.
From it arises the great principle, and then the origin of the elements. From the origin of the elements arises the vast, O joy of the Kurus.
From the vast comes Hari, my dear, and from Hari wolves also; the wise are robbed by the wolves; from this everything arises, O king. (text unclear)
In the same way, O best of kings, the awakening of these elemental measures swiftly follows in turn, O tiger of the Kurus.
From that also come the various senses, O best of kings. So this creation has been told, by worship, O joy of the Kurus.
Hear again, O best of kings, the detail of the elements here. All beings are rich in qualities, O lord of the earth.
Starting with space, each next one in order has one, two, three, four and five qualities.
Then the lord Brahma, seated on the lotus, the master,
from the words of the Veda made at the beginning the names, deeds and separate stations of all. The lord created the gods born of action, who have bodies.
He created the group of the Tushita gods, and the eternal sacrifice, O king. O hero, having given the secret eternal Brahman to his equals,
he milked out, for the success of sacrifice, the Rig, Yajus and Sama Vedas, and also time and its divisions, the planets and the seasons, O king,
rivers, seas and mountains, level and rough ground, desire, anger, speech and pleasure, O best of the Kurus.

He made creation, O best of kings, wishing to create many kinds of creatures. For discernment of actions he made right and wrong. He joined these creatures with pairs such as pleasure and pain. Tiny, perishable measures, said to be the halves of tens, [made the world].
By these, in due order, all this comes to be, O hero. Whatever action was done earlier by one set to it, O king,

first: स तदेव स्वयं भेजे सृज्यमानं पुनः पुनः ।
en: he himself takes up that same action again and again as he is created: harmful or harmless, gentle or cruel, right or wrong, true or false.
Whatever came to him in a creation enters him again by itself, as the seasons, with their signs, return of their own accord in turn.
So embodied beings take up their own deeds. For the growth of the world here, from the mouth, arms, thighs and feet,

first: ब्रह्म क्षत्रं तथा चोभौ वैश्यशूद्रौ नृपोत्तम ।
en: the Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya and Shudra were made, O best of kings. From those four mouths [of Brahma] the Vedas came forth.
The Rigveda collection, my dear, came with the great-souled Vasishtha, from the eastern mouth, and hear now of the southern one, O mighty-armed one.
The Yajurveda came with Yajnavalkya, O great king; the Samas from the western mouth, with the great sage Gautama.
The Atharvaveda came from the northern mouth, O best of kings, with the sage Shaunaka, honoured by the world.
And the fifth mouth, O mighty-armed one, famed in the world, from it came the eighteen Puranas with the histories, O descendant of Bharata,
O lift of the Kuru line; and other law books also, by Yama and others, honoured by the world.
Then the lord god divided his body in two. Having divided his body, with one half he became a man.
With the other half a woman, and in her the lord made Viraj. He, the Person, performed austerities and made Viraj.
He performed austerities, O king, wishing to create many kinds of creatures. First he made ten great sages, lords of creatures.

first: नारदं च भृगुं तात कं प्रचेतसमेव हि ।
en: Narada, Bhrigu, Ka, Prachetas, Pulaha, Kratu, Pulastya, Atri and Angiras,
and Marichi, O best of kings, who is the first Prajapati. He made these and others, O best of kings, of great brilliance.
Then he created gods, sages and demons, O joy of the Kurus, Yakshas, Rakshasas, Pishachas, Gandharvas, Apsarases and Asuras,

first: मनुष्याणां पितॄणां च सर्पाणां चैव भारत ।
en: and many groups of men, ancestors, serpents and Nagas, O descendant of Bharata, O mighty-armed one.
Lightning, thunderbolts, red rainbows, comets and meteors, and the groups of heavenly lights;
men, Kinnaras, fish, boars and birds, elephants, horses, cattle, deer and beasts of prey, O descendant of Bharata,
worms, insects, moths, lice, nits and bedbugs, every biting fly and mosquito, and the many kinds of plants.

first: एवं स भास्करो देवः ससर्ज भुवनत्रयम् ।
en: In this way the god Bhaskara, the sun, created the three worlds. What kind of action is told here for each being,
I will tell all that, and the order of their births. Elephants, beasts of prey, deer, my dear, and the different kinds of cattle,
Pishachas, men, and Rakshasas are born from the womb. Birds, serpents, crocodiles, fish and tortoises are egg-born.
Likewise all such creatures here, land-born and water-born, and those born of sweat: biting flies, mosquitoes, lice and bedbugs.
They are born of heat, and anything else like these. All plants, born by sprouting, grow from seed and stalk.
Herbs end when their fruit ripens, bearing fruit of many kinds. Those that bear fruit without flowers are called vanaspatis.
Trees are remembered as bearing both flowers and fruit. There are many kinds of clusters and shrubs, and kinds of grass,
creepers and vines growing from seed and stalk, wrapped in manifold darkness because of their past actions.
They have inner awareness and feel pleasure and pain. So many are the courses of birth that have arisen, O joy of the Kurus.
From that god, the radiant great-souled Bhaskara, they arise in this terrible, always moving cycle of rebirth, my dear.

first: एवं सर्वं स सृष्ट्वेदं राजँल्लोकगुरुं परम् ।
en: Having created all this, O king, the supreme teacher of the worlds, the self of all beings, vanished, wearing out time with time.

first: यदा स देवो जागर्ति तदेदं चेष्टते जगत् ।
en: When that god wakes, this world moves; when the peaceful one sleeps, everything closes its eyes.
When he sleeps, O best of kings, creatures, bound by their deeds, turn back from their own actions, and the mind sinks into weariness.
When all together dissolve in that great soul, then this self of all beings sleeps in comfort, O descendant of Bharata.

first: तमो यदा समाश्रित्य चिरं तिष्ठति सेन्द्रियः ।
en: When he stays long in darkness with his senses, he does no new action and leaves his bodily form.

first: यदाहंमात्रिको भूत्वा बीजं स्थास्नु चरिष्णु च ।
en: When he becomes only the sense of "I" and enters the seed, both still and moving, fully joined, then he lets go of the form.
So this lord, by waking and sleeping, ceaselessly gives life to this whole world and brings death to it, himself unchanging.

first: कल्पादौ सृजते तात अन्ते कल्पस्य संहरेत् ।
en: At the start of an age he creates, my dear, and at its end he withdraws. His day here is called the end of an age.
Now hear, O descendant of Bharata, the count of time of that age. Eighteen blinks of the eye are called a kashtha.
Thirty kashthas make a kala, and thirty kalas are remembered as a kshana. Those who know hours say twelve kshanas make a muhurta.
Thirty muhurtas are declared by the wise to be a day and night; thirty days and nights make a month; two months make a season.
Three seasons make a half-year; two half-years make a year. The sun divides days and nights into human and divine ones.
Night is for the sleep of beings, day for the activity of deeds. For the ancestors, night and day make a month, and the division is by the two fortnights.

first: कर्म चेष्टास्वहः कृष्णः मुक्तः स्वप्नाय शर्वरी ।
en: The day is for deeds and activity; the dark fortnight, and the night, for sleep. For the gods, night and day make a year, and their division is again as follows.
The day is the northern course of the sun, and the night the southern one. Now the measure of Brahma's night and day, O lord of the earth:
learn from me the ages one by one in order. Four thousand years are said to make the Krita age.
Its dawn is four hundred years, and its twilight is the same. The wise know the Treta as three thousand years.

first: शतानि षट् च राजेन्द्र सन्ध्यासन्ध्यांशयोः पृथक् ।
en: Six hundred years, O best of kings, are for its dawn and twilight separately. The Dvapara is declared to be two thousand years.
The wise say its dawn and twilight are four hundred. The Tishya [Kali] is told to be a thousand years with two hundred more.
This is the count of the four ages, O best of kings. Taken together, it is a set of four ages.
This is called a divine age of twelve thousand years. A thousand such divine ages by count
are to be known as one day of Brahma, and the night is said to be as long. Those who know say the holy day of Brahma ends after a thousand ages.
The people who know day and night say the night is of the same length. Then at the end of the ages, he who was asleep wakes.
Awake, he creates the mind, which is both being and non-being. Urged by the wish to create, the mind transforms creation.

first: विपुलं जायते तस्मात्तस्य शब्दं गुणं विदुः ।
en: From it arises the vast [space], whose quality the wise say is sound. From the vast, as it changes, comes the pure, scent-bearing

first: बलवाञ्जायते वायुः स वै स्पर्शगुणो मतः ।
en: powerful wind, which is held to have the quality of touch. From the wind, as it changes, comes the shining, darkness-removing
fire, of many-coloured rays, whose quality they say is form. From it, as it changes, the waters are remembered by the wise to be born.

first: तासां गुणो रसो ज्ञेयः सर्वलोकस्य भावनः।
en: The quality of the waters is to be known as taste, the nourisher of all the world. From the waters, the earth has the quality of smell. Such is the creation from the beginning.
The age of twelve thousand [divine years] told before, the Saumanasa age, multiplied seventy-one times, is here called a Manvantara.
Manvantaras are countless, and so are creation and dissolution. Still, in the day of Brahma there are always fourteen Manus.
They are always told by the learned by number, O tiger of the Kurus. Beside the Svayambhuva Manu here, six other Manus come from his line.
The mighty great souls created their own creatures. [The others are] Savarneya, Panchabhautya and Raucya.

first: एते भविष्या मनवः सप्त प्रोक्ता नृपोत्तम ।
en: These seven Manus, O best of kings, are said to be those to come. In their own periods they protect all this, moving and unmoving.
Such is the day of the great-souled Virinchi [Brahma]. At its end he makes creation, as I have told you.
The supreme one does this as if playing, O ruler of men. In the Krita age duty stands on all four feet, and so does truth.
No gain by wrong means comes to men. In the other ages, my dear, gains and duty [change], O joy of the Kurus,
as they decline, as the lord Manu says: through theft, falsehood and tricks, O king of boundless splendour.
In the Treta and later ages duty loses one quarter at a time. People were free of disease, all their aims were met, and they lived four hundred years.
In the Krita, Treta and the rest, their life span shrinks quarter by quarter, and so does the life told in the Vedas and the blessings of mortals, O joy of the Kurus.

first: कर्मणां तु फलं तात फलत्यनुयुगं सदा ।
en: The fruit of deeds, my dear, ripens in every age, and the power of embodied beings also bears fruit in the world.
The duties are one thing in the Krita age, another in the Treta, another after that in the Dvapara, and another for people in the Kali age, suited to the duty of each age.
Austerity is supreme in the Krita age, knowledge in the Treta; they say sacrifice in the Dvapara and giving alone in the Kali age.
To protect all creation, O radiant king, he assigned separate duties to those from the mouth, arms, thighs and feet.
Teaching, studying, performing sacrifice, conducting sacrifice for others, giving, and receiving gifts: these he assigned to Brahmins.
Protecting the people, O king, giving, studying, attachment to sense objects [in due measure] and offering sacrifice: these he assigned to the Kshatriya.
Guarding cattle, giving, sacrifice and study, trade, lending at interest and farming are for the Vaishya.

first: एकमेव तु शूद्रस्य कर्म लोके प्रकीर्तितम् ।
en: Only one work is declared for the Shudra in the world: service of these same classes in due order.
The part of a person above the navel is always the best, O best of kings. And even purer than that is the mouth of the self-born one.
"The Brahmin was born from the mouth": so says the Vedic scripture. By right, the Brahmin is the lord of all this duty.

first: स सृष्टो ब्रह्मणा पूर्वं तपस्तप्त्वा कुरूद्वह ।
en: He was made first by Brahma after austerities, O lift of the Kuru line, to guard the offerings to gods and to ancestors, and everything.
The dwellers in heaven eat the offerings through his mouth, and the ancestors their offerings. What is higher than that?
Of beings, the living are the best; of the living, those who live by understanding; of those with understanding, men; and among men, Brahmins are remembered as best.
Among Brahmins the learned; among the learned, those of settled mind; among these, those who act; among those who act, the knowers of Brahman.
The birth of a Brahmin, O best of kings, is said to be for the sake of duty here. Born for the success of all, he goes to Brahma's hall, O king.
And being born, he is born on earth for the welfare of beings and to guard the treasury of duty.
All that is on earth belongs to the Brahmin. By his excellent birth, the Brahmin deserves all this.

first: स्वकीयं ब्राह्मणो भुङ्क्ते विदधाति च सुव्रत ।
en: The Brahmin eats his own and gives, O one of good vows. Other people live eating what he, in his kindness, lets them have.
The Brahmin can bring about the rise or fall of the other three classes, O king, without doubt. When pleased, he brings prosperity.
When angry, he brings ruin; therefore he is most worthy of honour. When a Brahmin is present, no one else has lordship, O king.
He acts from desire and goes where he wishes, O best of kings. From that [he reaches] the city of the gods, and then greater glory.
From the world of glory he goes to the world of Janas and to Brahma's world. The Brahmin attains the state of Brahman, O mighty-armed one, without doubt.
The state of Brahman is hard to reach, O one of good vows, in the worlds of Brahma.

first: ब्रह्मत्वं कीदृशं विप्रो ब्रह्मलोकं च गच्छति ।
en: What is the state of Brahman like? How does a Brahmin go to Brahma's world? Is a Brahmin only a name? What are the qualities by which he reaches the state of Brahman? Tell me, O Brahmin, how it is gained.

first: साधुसाधु महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः ॥ १४१ ॥
en: Well said, well said, O mighty-armed one. Hear my excellent answer.

first: ये प्रोक्ता वेदशास्त्रेषु संस्कारा ब्राह्मणस्य तु ।
en: The rites of refinement told in the Vedas and law books for a Brahmin, beginning with conception, those that belong to him, O king,

forty and eight, completed according to scripture, O king: he reaches the place of Brahma and the state of a Brahmin, O giver of honour. These rites are in every way the cause of the state of Brahman, without doubt.

first: संस्काराः के मता ब्रह्मन्ब्रह्मत्वे ब्राह्मणस्य तु ।
en: Which rites are held to lead a Brahmin to the state of Brahman, O Brahmin? Tell me, O tiger of the twice-born, for my curiosity is great.

first: साधुसाधु महाबाहो शृणु मे परमं वचः ।
en: Well said, well said, O mighty-armed one. Hear my excellent answer. The rites told in the Vedas and law books for a Brahmin, declared by the wise, O mighty-armed one, hear all of them in full.
Conception, the rite for a male child, the parting of the hair, birth rite, first feeding, tonsure and initiation, O king,
the four Vedic vows, then the bath [ending study], marriage with a wife of the same duty, and the sacrifices, O giver of honour,
are said to be the duty of five, for one's own good, O king: of gods, ancestors, men, [other] beings, and the Brahmin.
Of these are also the Ashtaka rite and the Parvana ancestor offering, and the Shravani, Agrahayani, Chaitri and Ashvayuji rites.
Also the seven cooked-food sacrifices, the setting up of the fires and the good rites, the daily fire offering, O king, and the new-moon sacrifice at the moon's disappearance,

first: पौर्णमासं च राजेन्द्र चातुर्मास्यानि चापि हि ।
en: the full-moon sacrifice, O best of kings, the four-monthly sacrifices, the animal sacrifice and Sautramani.

first: हविर्यज्ञास्तथा सप्त तेषां चापि हि सत्क्रिया ।
en: The seven offering sacrifices, and their good rites: Agnishtoma, Atyagnishtoma, Ukthya and Shodashi are known,
Vajapeya, Atiratra and Aptoryama, as remembered. The seven Soma sacrifices stand among the rites, O lift of the Kuru line.
These are the forty rites of the twice-born, O best of kings. And there are eight qualities of the self, my dear; hear them too, O descendant of Bharata.
Freedom from envy, compassion, patience, freedom from strain, auspiciousness, generosity, purity and freedom from greed, O lift of the Kurus.
These eight qualities, my dear, are named by the wise. Hear fully the mark of each, O hero.
One who neither harms the good qualities of the virtuous, nor praises his own qualities, nor rejoices at others' faults, is said to be free from envy.

first: अपरे बन्धुवर्गे वा मित्रे द्वेष्टरि वा सदा ।
en: Behaviour toward strangers, relatives, friends or enemies as toward oneself, is called compassion.

first: वाचा मनसि काये च दुःखेनोत्पादितेन च ।
en: Not becoming angry or resentful when pain is caused by word, mind or body, is called patience.
Avoiding forbidden food, keeping company with the blameless, and standing firm in right conduct: this is called purity.

first: शरीरं पीड्यते येन शुभेनापि च कर्मणा ।
en: One should not do, to excess, any act, even a good one, that torments the body. That is called freedom from strain.
Always doing praiseworthy things and avoiding the blameworthy: this is what sages who speak of Brahman call auspiciousness.
Giving even a little each day, with an unbroken mind, is called generosity.
Being content with whatever one has, even if small, and not harming others' property: this is called freedom from greed.

first: वपुर्यस्य तु इत्येतैः संस्कारैः संस्कृतं द्विजः ।
en: A twice-born whose body is refined by these rites, having gained the state of Brahman here, goes to Brahma's world.
By holy Vedic rites, beginning with conception, for the twice-born, the rites of refining the body should be done; they purify here and after death.
Having then gained purity of birth, and the duty marked by the stages of life, one reaches liberation without doubt, according to this Purana, O best of kings.
Brahmins, O tiger of the Kurus, are without doubt desired, especially by those who depend on them and are always speaking blessings.
One who, leaving aside the twice-born near him, honours other twice-born, incurs sin through that insult; it cannot be told.
Therefore one who is near should always be honoured by rule, O king. In the same way one should honour guests with gifts of food, drink and the like.
The Brahmin is the eldest, best and highest of all classes. In this way, in this Purana, the rites of a Brahmin [are told].

first: शृणोति यश्च जानाति यश्चापि पठते सदा ।
en: One who hears, knows or always recites this gains here prosperity, growth, fame and supreme fortune.
Wealth, grain, glory, sons, relatives and good looks; having reached the world of the sun, one will attain Brahma's world.
